html:
The last leader of the Soviet Union, from 1985 to 1991. His reforms opened up the country and ended the Cold War, and led, against his wishes, to the Soviet Union's breakup.

Born to a peasant family in southern Russia in 1931, he rose through the Communist Party and became its General Secretary in 1985. The economy was stagnant and the war in Afghanistan dragged on. His answer had two parts:

  • glasnost, openness: freer speech and press and an honest look at the past;
  • perestroika, restructuring of the economy and politics.

The Chernobyl disaster of 1986 pushed him further toward openness. He signed arms treaties with Ronald Reagan, pulled Soviet troops out of Afghanistan, and in 1989 did not send tanks when Eastern Europe threw off communism and the Berlin Wall fell.

At home, reform loosened the state without fixing the economy, and the republics pushed for independence. After a failed hardline coup in August 1991, he resigned on 25 December as the Soviet Union dissolved.
sum: The last leader of the Soviet Union, from 1985 to 1991. His reforms opened up the country and ended the Cold War, and led, against his wishes, to the Soviet Union's breakup.
